definitions.explanation: A speech sound produced without obstruction of airflow. Japanese has five vowels: あ (a), い (i), う (u), え (e), お (o).

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{母音|ぼいん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{五|いつ}つ→五つ：02892_itsutsu⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧{母音|ぼいん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{数|かず}→数：00204_kazu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: English has more vowels than Japanese.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{母音|ぼいん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{連続|れんぞく}する→連続する：22173_renzokusuru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{発音|はつおん}→発音：01698_hatsuon⟧しにくく⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: In Japanese, when vowels occur in succession, they can become difficult to pronounce.

notes:
USAGE:
A linguistics and language-learning term. Useful when discussing pronunciation differences between Japanese and other languages. Japanese vowels are "pure" (monophthongs), unlike English vowels which often glide (diphthongs).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {母音|ぼいん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{発音|はつおん}→発音：01698_hatsuon⟧: vowel pronunciation
- {長母音|ちょうぼいん}: long vowel
- {短母音|たんぼいん}: short vowel
- {母音|ぼいん}⟦{調和|ちょうわ}→調和：05216_chouwa⟧: vowel harmony

CONTRASTING TERM:
- ⟦{子音|しいん}→子音：18405_shiin⟧: consonant
